Bakery east frontage aisle (customer) — the 1.1 m perimeter aisle between the east faces of the bakery display boxes (x=1121.4-1143.6 and the southern box at x=1136.0-1148.5) and the west face of the east-wall bakery case run (x=1161.5). The BAKERY seal disk (pt 1190.8,492.5 r=130) bridges gaps <= 12 pt, and this aisle narrows to 11.7 pt in exactly two places, so the bridge closed it there and the resulting slivers were culled BELOW the 100-cell reporting floor — silently, with no entry in report.json culled_pockets: (a) y=412-416 where the two east-wall door leaves are drawn swung open into the aisle (leaf strokes (1155.7,402.6)-(1161.3,391.4) and (1155.5,416.1)-(1161.4,405.0), each with its swing arc), leaving 1143.6->1155.3 clear; (b) y=570 at the south-east corner of the last display box (east face 1148.5), leaving 1148.5->1161.5. Both cut a printed, walkable customer aisle in half: the segment y=418-534 was left reachable only from the south end of the produce/bakery case run and the segment y=542-568 only from its north end, a ~9 m detour each. An open door leaf is not a wall — the floor in front of the bakery cases is shoppable end to end. Rect = that aisle over the full length of the case run (y=380-576), west edge at x=1145.0 so the grid column it starts on is the first one clear of the box faces (starting at 1143.6 nibbled 2 pt off the box gaps and shrank the dead-slot pocket 313 -> 301 cells), east edge at x=1156.0 — the west extent of the leaf strokes — because the 2 pt slot BEHIND a swung-open leaf (x=1158) is genuinely unusable and restoring it only adds 2- and 3-cell orphan pockets (components went 1 -> 3 on the first attempt). It restores only cells the drawing already left blank, so the leaf strokes themselves, the 0.70 m dead slot west of the boxes (x=1112-1120, the 313-cell pocket) and the east-wall run all stay blocked
